hypothesis: The Riemann-Roch solver beat Semaev, but it has never been run against the DUMBEST possible decomposition oracle on the same factor base: enumerate every unordered pair of factor-base points and test whether the residual R - P1 - P2 lands in the factor base. The background note's falsification target is stated against exhaustive search over the oracle's own candidate set, not against Semaev, and this control has been absent from every round of this thread. Prediction, stated before running: the RR solver LOSES to it, because solver_10 counted about 3,400 candidate functions per target at d = 6 while the pair enumeration over the same base has only about 1,400 pairs, and each RR candidate costs hundreds of field operations against a pair test's handful.
why_this_is_the_null_object: docs/inventor-protocol.md requires a null-object control before belief. 'Better than Semaev-via-SAT' is a claim about two algebraic encodings under one SAT solver; it is not evidence that the encoding beats brute force. If the null object wins, the RR family's measured advantage is a statement about the comparator, and the honest reading of solver_10 changes.
curve: K_0 : y^2 + xy = x^3 + 1 over GF(2^131) in the repository's permuted type-II ONB model, group order checked against the Koblitz recurrence as 4r with the published 129-bit prime. Identical to solver_10.
targets: The EXACT targets of solver_10, read back from its committed raw.jsonl panel records -- both strata, all four targets each, with their planted triples. No reselection, no fresh sampling. This is a re-measurement of the same instances by a different oracle.
factor_base: Identical to solver_10: F = { P in E(GF(2^131)) : x(P) in V \ {0} }, V the span of the first d ONB basis vectors. Both lifts of each admissible abscissa are in F, so |F| = 2 * (number of admissible abscissas). Arity m = 3, abscissas pairwise distinct, none equal to 0 or to x(R).
method: For each unordered pair {P1, P2} of factor-base points with distinct abscissas, compute Q = R - P1 - P2 by the curve group law and accept when x(Q) lies in V \ {0} and differs from x(P1), x(P2). Every field operation goes through the same CountedField used by solver_10, so the operation counts are in the same unit and directly comparable. No algebra, no polynomial system, no solver: this is the control, and it is meant to be stupid.
validation: (1) Group order check as in solver_10. (2) Every accepted triple re-verified independently by lifting its abscissas and recomputing the signed group sum. (3) CROSS-ORACLE EQUALITY: on every d = 6 instance where solver_10's quadratic-image run reported status 'complete', the pair oracle's complete solution set must equal that run's solution set exactly. Two independent oracles disagreeing on a complete set is a correctness failure in one of them and invalidates the round. (4) On planted targets the planted triple must appear.
primary_metric: Counted field API operations to exhaust the candidate space for one target, and operations per verified relation, matched against solver_10's numbers on the same targets. Wall clock is reported but is secondary: the two implementations are both Python and neither is optimised.
falsification: The hypothesis of this contract is falsified if the pair oracle needs MORE counted field operations than the quadratic-image solver to exhaust the same instance. It is falsified in the other direction -- that is, confirmed -- if it needs materially fewer. A cross-oracle disagreement on any complete set invalidates the round regardless of cost.
limits: Both oracles are priced on the SAME factor base and arity, so this comparison says which oracle to use at a given (m, l); it says nothing about the attack, whose cost the product law relations x targets x oracle = m*2^n holds constant. The pair oracle's cost is C(|F|,2) per target by construction and its memory is O(|F|); it is the free-oracle floor's honest neighbour, not a new algorithm, and beating the RR solver with it is not an ECDLP result. Python ONB arithmetic is uncalibrated against the repository's Rust/GPU cost model. Counted field operations weight additions, multiplications and squarings equally and expand inversions; the two oracles have different primitive mixes, so a ratio near one would not be decisive -- only a large gap is.
